title: Trade only this FVG 📉
description:
Most traders see a Fair Value Gap and instantly look for an entry.

The problem? Not every FVG is worth trading.

Context matters. Structure matters. Liquidity matters.

In this video, you'll learn why some FVGs should be ignored and how to identify the ones that actually have a higher probability of working.

#trading #smc #forex #daytrading #fvg
spoken_transcript:
Kind: captions
Language: en
Just because a trade wins, doesn't mean
it is valid. Here's why these two
winning shorts are wrong and only one is
the high probability setup.
Price is initially in an uptrend. It
makes a high, then started reversing.
Before dropping, it leaves a fair value
gap near the last higher low.
Many traders would short this
retracement into the gap. But this trade
is invalid. Why?
Because there was no structure shift. No
proof the trend has actually changed.
The bias is still bullish.
Price drops further and now we get a
market structure shift. So bias becomes
bearish. But this next short is still
invalid. Why?
Because price didn't leave an imbalance
before the breakout. No fair value gap,
no entry point. Then price breaks lower
again. We get a true bearish break of
structure.
And this time price leaves a clean fair
value gap. We mark the zone for a
potential entry.
When price reaches the zone, we enter
short. Stop loss above the recent high,
target at the next liquidity pool, here
the low of the day.
Smart money is not about taking every
move. It's about taking the ones most
likely to win.
